Reports that ask for whole-number currency amounts are coming out with full floating point precision. Asking intcomma for a value rounded to zero decimal places returns the unrounded number instead: 1234.5454545 comes back as "1,234.5454545" when it should be "1,235". Asking for one, two or ten decimal places works correctly, and so does leaving the argument out entirely. Fix humanize/number.py. Leaving the digit count unset, or setting it explicitly to nothing, must continue to return the value with its precision untouched - that path is relied on elsewhere and must not start rounding.

metric() blows up on a value of zero. Instead of returning a formatted string it raises ValueError with a math domain error, because the exponent that chooses the SI prefix is taken from the base-10 logarithm of the magnitude, and that is undefined at zero. Any caller rendering a series of readings therefore dies the moment one of them is zero, in every mode - with a unit, without one, and at any precision. Fix humanize/number.py so zero renders the way any other value needing no prefix does: the mantissa formatted to the requested precision, no prefix letter, and the unit appended under the usual spacing rule, which omits the space for a degree sign. That means a constant string is not an acceptable answer, because the precision and the unit both still have to be honoured. Nothing else may change: values that already format correctly, including the fallback to scientific notation beyond the prefix range, must be left exactly as they are, and the public signature must stay as it is.

The @throttle decorator in funcy/flow.py is documented to take a period, and callers have started passing that period as a datetime.timedelta instead of a plain number of seconds because it reads better at the call site. It does not work: decorating a function with a timedelta period blows up immediately with a TypeError, before the decorated function has been called even once, so the module fails to import wherever someone has written it that way. A numeric period is unaffected and behaves correctly. Make a timedelta period behave exactly like the equivalent number of seconds, including fractional periods such as half a second and long periods of a day or more. The public signature must not change - throttle still takes one argument and returns a decorator - and the existing numeric behaviour, including the fact that the deadline is computed from time.time(), must stay exactly as it is.

The booking report adds interval lengths straight up, so a room held twice from nine to ten reads as two hours occupied, and there is no way at all to answer the question the front desk asks, which is when the room is free. Add merge(intervals) and complement(intervals, window) to the intervals module. merge returns a new sorted list holding the fewest intervals covering exactly the same points: overlapping ones join, and so do ones that merely touch, since half-open [0,10) and [10,20) already describe [0,20). It takes its input in any order, nested and duplicated, must not modify the sequence it was given, and returns an empty list for an empty input. complement returns the parts of window that none of the intervals covers, in ascending order, clipped to the window and ignoring anything wholly outside it; the complement of no intervals is the window itself, an interval spanning the whole window gives an empty list, and two touching intervals leave no gap between them rather than a zero-length one. Nothing already in the package may change.

Our clients retry on a flat delay, so an upstream brown-out has the whole fleet retrying in lockstep. Add exponential backoff, a ceiling and optional full jitter to call_with_retry and to the retry decorator in src/retry.py as four keyword-only options, named and defaulted exactly: backoff=1.0, max_delay=None, jitter=False, rng=None. The wait after the n-th failure (n from 1) is delay * backoff ** (n - 1), then clamped to max_delay when that is not None, then - only when jitter - replaced by rng.uniform(0.0, wait) on the already-clamped value; that float is what sleeper gets. rng must be injectable: any object exposing uniform(a, b), falling back to a module-level random.Random when None. A backoff below 1.0 or a negative max_delay must raise ValueError from call_with_retry before the first attempt. The defaults must reproduce today's behaviour exactly - at backoff=1.0, max_delay=None and jitter=False every wait is still exactly delay - and existing parameter names, exception order and the injected sleeper must not change. README.md repeats this design note.
